RagShortTexts: The Fairs of Champagne connected northern cloth manufacturing with southern Mediterranean.

Variants.Content: Rotating through Troyes, Provins, and Bar-sur-Aube, the Champagne Fairs formed the commercial clearinghouse of 13th-century Europe. Northern Flemish broadcloth met Mediterranean spices, silks, and alum. Protected by the Counts of Champagne with royal safe-conducts, Italian bankers introduced the bill of exchange, revolutionizing credit.

The Counts of Champagne grew exceedingly wealthy purely through market rents, weighmaster fees, and hall tolls. Even in wartime, sovereigns shield fairbound merchants, preserving the continent's financial engine.
Behind money-changers' benches, Sienese and Florentine bankers assay silver mark fineness. Commercial contracts recorded by licensed fair notaries hold legal validity from London to Palermo.
